$comment: Welcome tour and short focused tours (D294 proposed). Plain words for new users. Each step points at a part of the studio window by anchor name; a step whose anchor is not on screen is skipped.

steps.title: Scenes
steps.text: A scene is one complete look for your stream: where your game, camera and graphics sit. Double-click a scene to switch to it. The + button adds one; right-click a scene to copy or rename it.

steps.title: Layers
steps.text: Layers are the things inside a scene: the game, your camera, text and pictures. Pick one to move or resize it. H and V choose which of the two pictures you are editing.

steps.title: Add and copy layers
steps.text: The + button adds a layer. Right-click a layer to copy, rename or remove it.

steps.title: Horizontal picture (H)
steps.text: This is the wide picture for YouTube and your recordings. What you see here is what your viewers get.

steps.title: Vertical picture (V)
steps.text: This is the tall picture for vertical videos. Keep the important parts inside it so nothing gets cut off.

steps.title: Look
steps.text: Select a layer, then use Look to round its corners, add a shadow or a filter. Move the sliders and watch the previews.

steps.title: Audio mixer
steps.text: One strip for each sound: game, microphone, music. Mute a strip, or press CUE to hear only that sound in your headphones while your viewers hear nothing extra.

steps.title: Start stream
steps.text: This goes live. Ujwalam asks you to type a confirmation first, so you can never go live by accident.

steps.title: Record
steps.text: Record saves your show to a file on this PC. Press it again to stop.

steps.title: Save clip
steps.text: Saves the last 60 seconds, in both the wide and the tall picture, as clip files. Use it right after something great happens.

steps.title: Mark moment
steps.text: Marks this exact moment so the clip maker looks at it first. Press it when you think a clip is coming.

steps.title: Status chips
steps.text: These show what is on right now: Live, Recording, and Clips. Red means on. The Clips chip tells you when Ujwalam is making clips.

steps.title: What happens behind the scenes
steps.text: When Ujwalam works on something in the background, such as cutting clips or saving settings, a Tasks button appears here at the top right. Click it for the list. It never blocks you.

steps.title: My clips
steps.text: Opens the folder with your finished clips.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Choose when clips are made, which matches get clips, and where files are saved. Tips and this tour can be switched back on under Help and tips.

steps.title: Need help later?
steps.text: Press ? any time to see how clips are made and how posting works, or to replay this tour.

steps.title: You can point out a moment
steps.text: Press Mark moment when something good happens. The clip maker looks at marked moments first.

steps.title: Or save the last minute
steps.text: Save clip keeps the last 60 seconds, wide and tall, right away.

steps.title: The Clips chip
steps.text: It tells you if Ujwalam is waiting for your answer, making clips, or done. Hover it to see your choices.

steps.title: Progress
steps.text: While clips are made, the Tasks button here opens each step and its progress: reading the game screen, then making clip videos, with the time left.

steps.title: Where clips go
steps.text: Finished clips are saved in this folder.

steps.title: Your choices
steps.text: In Settings, Clips, choose when to make clips and which matches count, for example only matches where you finish in the top 3.

steps.title: Start from your clips
steps.text: Posting works on finished clips. They are saved in this folder first.

steps.title: The Posts view
steps.text: Open More. If Posts is in the list, posting is switched on in this build. It shows one package per clip to read and approve.

steps.title: Switches
steps.text: Posting is off until you turn it on under Settings, Advanced. Turning it on asks you to type a confirmation.

steps.title: What is built
steps.text: Press ? and open Posting your clips to see exactly what works today and what still needs your yes.
